item.title: Benekiva Introduces Kiva Claims Assistant
item.description: (Image source: Benekiva/IIR.) Benekiva (Des Moines, Iowa) has introduced Kiva, an AI Smart Claims Assistant embedded in the company’s Claims Workbench. “We built Kiva to provide another set of eyes within the workflow to help someone recognize a missing requirement or see what needs attention next.” Benekiva positions Kiva as an assistive tool rather than an independent claims decision-maker, with human judgment remaining central to the process. “It should be how much unnecessary work we can take off their plate so they can spend more attention on the decisions and people who need it.” Kiva is available as part of the Benekiva Claims Workbench.

item.title: Fitch upgrades Beazley’s rating, cites strategic importance to Zurich
item.description: The deal creates a huge, global specialty insurance business, with Zurich CEO Mario Greco stating previously that by 2029, “the integration of Beazley will generate incremental revenue growth of over $1 billion per annum.” Fitch’s upgrades reflect its assessment of Beazley’s strategic importance to Zurich, which it determines as ‘Very Important.’ “This results in a two-notch uplift from Beazley’s standalone credit quality of ‘a+’ for its IFS Rating, given ZIG’s stronger credit quality. After Zurich Insurance Group completed its 100% acquisition of specialist insurer Beazley, Fitch Ratings has upgraded the Insurer Financial Strength (IFS) Rating of Beazley Insurance DAC to ‘AA’ from ‘A+’, and also upgraded the Long-Term Issuer Default Ratings (IDRs) of the Dublin subsidiary and Beazley plc to ‘AA-‘ from ‘A’. Today, Fitch, a global credit rating agency, alongside upgrading Beazley Insurance DAC’s IFS Rating and Beazley’s IDRs, has removed the rating from Rating Watch Positive, and confirmed that the outlooks are stable.

item.title: Cat bond risk spreads fall 9.5% in September, but rising risk free rate helps to offset: Plenum
item.description: Catastrophe bond insurance risk spreads declined by 9.5% during the month of September 2026 as wind seasonality took hold, but with treasury yields having risen the increase to the risk free rate of return on collateral served to offset the impact to the cat bond market coupon available to investors, the latest data on cat bond yields from Plenum Investments shows. Cat bond insurance risk spreads ended September 25th at 4.57%, down 9.5% from the August 28th figure of 5.05%. But, at the same time, with treasury yields rising and this being the collateral of choice in the catastrophe bond market, this risk-free component of investors returns has risen as well.

item.title: KCC updates and enhances US Severe Convective Storm model
item.description: Catastrophe risk modelling specialist Karen Clark & Company (KCC), has launched a new version of its US Severe Convective Storm (SCS) model, incorporating a range of advancements that further strengthens the firm’s approach to quantifying losses from one of the weather perils driving a significant share of insured property losses across the country. “Version 5.0 reflects ongoing investments in atmospheric science, engineering, AI, and actual claims-based verification to continually refine the representation of severe convective storm risk.” View all of our Artemis Live video interviews and subscribe to our podcast . KCC noted that Version 5.0 of its US SCS model includes refined techniques for severe tornado outbreaks, as well as improved tornado and wind intensity calculations along the Southeast coast.

item.title: CatIQ lifts industry loss estimate for Ontario-Quebec storms to CAD 491m
item.description: CatIQ, a Toronto-domiciled organisation providing industry-wide catastrophe insurance data and a subsidiary of PERILS, has disclosed an elevated third industry loss estimate of CAD 491 million for the severe thunderstorm event that struck parts of southern Ontario and southern Quebec between 30 June and 3 July 2026. CatIQ explained that the loss estimate covers property, both commercial and residential, and vehicle (motor) claims, including additional loss adjustment expenses. All told, more than 70% of the incurred total and more than 60% of claims for personal property arose from Nepean and communities on the southwest side of Ottawa.” The next update for the Ontario and Quebec storm estimate will be released on 5 January 2027, following the PERILS reporting schedule.

item.title: LMG Data Council expands Core Data Record to cover full insurance lifecycle
item.description: The London Market Group’s (LMG) Data Council, the governing body representing London market brokers, underwriters, and Lloyd’s that sets data standards for market modernisation, has updated the Core Data Record (CDR) to introduce First Notification of Loss (FNOL) claims data, establishing the market’s first direct digital link between claims and placing contract information. Together, these updates help firms to share data based on agreed standards across the insurance lifecycle, a significant milestone for digital delivery in the London market, LMG Data Council highlighted. Joe Brace, Chair of the Data Council and Operations Director at the Lloyd’s Market Association, said: “For the first time, we have provided a market-wide set of data standards for all contract types (open market and delegated, facultative and treaty etc), all classes of business, and including guidance for pre-bind data, not just post-bind and accounting.

item.title: TWIA forecasts $2.05bn reinsurance and cat bond need for 2027, down 10%
item.description: The Texas Windstorm Insurance Association (TWIA) is forecasting a roughly 10% reduction in its reinsurance and catastrophe bond needs for 2027, as its Catastrophe Reserve Trust Fund (CRTF) is projected to grow from $25 million this year to as much as $350 million ahead of the renewals. Preliminary 2027 budget information is being presented to the TWIA Board this week, based on projected exposures, the expected attachment point and prevailing reinsurance and catastrophe bond market conditions. The association is also forecasting a 2027 risk transfer budget of around $173 million, nearly 18% below this year’s almost $210 million, with softer reinsurance and catastrophe bond pricing expected to help reduce costs.

item.title: Don’t Sweat the Heatwave, El Niño Is Cooking up Some Raucous Weather for California
item.description: Most of the attention on California’s weather is focused right now on an unusual October heat wave with triple-digit temperatures in some areas, but talk of “atmospheric rivers” bringing crashing waves, pounding rain and snow by the feet to the mountains may soon take center stage. Warnings are mounting as El Niño conditions strengthen based on oceanic and atmospheric observations, and NOAA is reporting a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event this fall and winter, with a seasonal outlook that favors above-normal precipitation across Southern California. AccuWeather released its 2026-2027 United States Winter Forecast on Wednesday, which predicts that “a very strong El Niño may reach historic levels in December or January and will be a major influence through winter and into early spring 2027.” Related: California’s El Niño Emergency Begins Now as Beaches Erode AccuWeather meteorologists say it has the potential to be the strongest El Niño since 1950.

item.title: Iran Ramps Up Ship Attacks in Hormuz as Oil, Gas Flows Rise
item.description: Iran has increased the pace of attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, just as oil shipments through the world’s most important energy chokepoint approach prewar levels. Brent crude rose 0.8% to over $101 a barrel in early Asian trading as investors weighed increased flows through the Strait of Hormuz against a pickup in Iranian attacks on vessels. UK Maritime Trade Operations has reported nine attacks in the waterway already this month, half the total number it reported for all of September in the Strait of Hormuz and Persian Gulf combined.

item.title: Tinubu introduces conversational configuration

item.title: XPT Specialty launches Texas homeowners program

The launch expands XPT’s personal lines offering as severe weather exposure and rising rebuilding costs continue to constrain homeowners capacity in Texas.

item.title: rrelentless launches Zurich-backed haulage insurance

The product targets UK haulage fleets with 10 to 75 vehicles at inception.

item.title: Bermuda Insurance Executive and Mother Were on Missing Medical Flight to Boston
item.description: The two passengers aboard an air ambulance that crashed in the waters off Massachusetts over the weekend while flying from Bermuda to Boston were identified Monday as a mother from Bermuda and her son, an executive with Hamilton Re. Bermuda police said Marilyn Lavonne Bean, 66, and Sergio Wayne Lottimore, 41, both Bermudian nationals, were aboard a Gulfstream G100 along with four crew members when it went missing off Nantucket around 1 a.m. Bermuda is about 750 to 780 miles (roughly 1,200 to 1,250 kilometers) southeast of Boston.

item.title: CatIQ lifts Ontario & Quebec thunderstorm insured market loss estimate 12% to C$491m
item.description: CatIQ, Canada’s insured loss and exposure index provider, has raised its insurance industry loss estimate for the severe thunderstorm event that impacted parts of southern Ontario and southern Quebec between June 30th and July 3rd, 2026, to CAD $491 million, a 12% increase from the firm’s second loss estimate of $439 million. CatIQ also confirmed that it will publish an updated loss estimate for the severe thunderstorm event on January 5th, 2027. CatIQ published its initial loss estimate from the event back in early August, putting the total at the time at $374 million.

item.title: US title insurance premiums rise 13% in 2025 as growth continues, reports AM Best
item.description: AM Best, the credit rating agency and provider of insurance industry research and analysis, has reported continued growth in the US title insurance market, with premiums increasing by 13% in 2025 and further gains recorded during the opening quarter of 2026. AM Best said its composite of title insurers recorded an 18% increase in direct premiums written in the first quarter of 2026 compared with the corresponding period in 2025. “With interest rates likely to remain higher for longer, activity on the residential side will likely be limited and leave the possibility for title insurance premium growth to be tied squarely to the commercial real estate market.” Financial performance across the title insurance segment also improved during 2025.

item.title: Markel International raises London Fine Art & Specie capacity to $250m
item.description: Markel Insurance, the insurance operation within Markel Group Inc., has raised its London Fine Art & Specie capacity from USD 100 million to USD 250 million through Lloyd’s of London to accommodate rising demand. Danny O’Donoghue, Head of Fine Art & Specie, Markel International, commented, “Clients are increasingly requiring larger limits due to rising valuations of fine art collections, significant increases in precious metals values and greater concentrations of high-value assets. The move also strengthens Markel’s ability to support larger and more complex Fine Art & Specie risks.

item.title: Pacific Life Re completes $3bn longevity reinsurance agreement with American National
item.description: Pacific Life Re, the global reinsurance business of Pacific Life, has announced the successful execution of a $3 billion longevity reinsurance agreement with American National Insurance Company. Adding: “This transaction highlights our ability to deliver tailored longevity solutions at scale and demonstrates our strong commitment to support PRT markets and policyholders worldwide.” Howie Timothy, AVP Client Solutions, North America, Savings & Retirement, Pacific Life Re, stated: “We are very proud to have partnered closely with American National on this deal and to showcase our capabilities and expertise in a new market. We look forward to continued partnership with the team at American National.” Pacific Life Re were supported on the deal by global law firm Eversheds Sutherland.

item.title: Data Centers Pump $340M Into Rural Texas Projects
item.description: As data centers move into the state at a rapid pace, Texas communities in mostly rural areas face a fiscal cliff from property tax cuts, inflation and overall economic uncertainty. These are just some of the public investments data center companies have paid for across rural Texas in the past year. The Texas Tribune reviewed news releases, public meeting agendas and interviewed local officials to understand how data centers are using their money in Texas.

item.title: Missouri AG Secures $42K Judgment Against Contractor Accused of Fraud
item.description: Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway announced that her office secured a jury conviction against Daniel Eschliman for scamming an elderly couple out of more than $42,000. Eschliman was criminally charged in one other contractor fraud case and has been sued civilly numerous times. The case was investigated by the Attorney General’s Office’s Consumer Protection Section after the victims filed a complaint against Eschliman.

item.title: Thousands of European Wind, Solar Power Systems Exposed Online: Dutch Researchers
item.description: Thousands of administrative systems at wind and solar power parks in Europe are exposed to the internet, potentially giving attackers access to interfaces that can stop turbines and raising the risk of sabotage, Dutch researchers warned on Tuesday . “If you can turn off the energy within the city or the airport, imagine that at a larger scale.” Using machine learning to sort and cluster data, the pair said they identified 8,547 internet-facing systems they could link to at specific solar parks (7,942) and wind farms (605) in 35 European countries, which should not have been exposed to the internet. The exposed systems included administrative and login interfaces as well as operational interfaces showing data and controls.

item.title: Heffernan acquires Walterry Insurance Brokers
item.description: Heffernan Insurance has acquired Walterry Insurance Brokers, an independent agency based in Clinton, Maryland. The Walterry team joined Heffernan effective May 1, 2026. Founded in 1968, Walterry specializes in media liability, professional liability and business insurance, serving newspapers, broadcasters, film and television producers, and nonprofit trade associations.

item.title: Grinnell files trademark application for “Farmutual”

Grinnell also previously used the FarMutual name in its member branding. Filed on October 1, 2026, the application has not yet been assigned to an examiner.

item.title: 2027 Insurance Trends: The Math is Getting More Complicated
item.description: Heading into 2027, some of the math is getting particularly complicated in ways we haven’t seen before. This ultimately makes some of the less flashy changes happening across insurance more important than ever. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety notes that vehicles equipped with crash-avoidance sensors can cost more to repair after comparable crashes because sensors themselves are expensive and often require calibration after replacement.

item.title: Trump Names Intelligence Chief Clayton as AI Czar, to Head Task Force
item.description: Trump, who has pushed to rename artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” said Clayton would head the newly created Super Intelligence Force (SIF), overseeing the government’s engagement with consumers, religious groups, AI companies and other stakeholders. In addition to Clayton, the task force’s leaders will include Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor, Trump wrote. US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton the administration’s AI czar, tasking him with coordinating the federal government’s efforts to maintain US leadership in the technology.

item.title: Large Commercial Property Rates Drop 14.5% in Q2 to Highlight Latest Willis Report
item.description: Commercial property rates continues to soften, according to a new report from Willis, a WTW business. Large and complex property rates with WTW’s portfolio dropped 14.5% in the second quarter of 2026, according to the fall 2026 edition of its Insurance Marketplace Realities report. The report examines dozens of lines of commercial business in North America.
